STEP 1 - Scene: A single slice of pepperoni pizza on a white square plate, photographed from above at a near-overhead angle. The slice shows a crust edge, tomato sauce, melted cheese, and pepperoni.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is a square white plate about 26 cm across. Vessel area ≈ 26 x 26 ≈ 676 cm² (use ~530 cm² for a round-equivalent; I use the square area directly at ~600 cm² of usable surface).

STEP 3 - Items: (1) pizza crust, (2) tomato sauce, (3) mozzarella cheese, (4) pepperoni (2 slices visible, one whole-ish disc).

STEP 4 - Area: The pizza slice spans roughly 190 px by 150 px in a plate roughly 440 px wide, so the slice is about 12% of the plate's visible width-squared. Estimated coverage: whole slice ≈ 8% of plate area. Crust ≈ 3%, sauce ≈ 2%, cheese ≈ 2.5%, pepperoni ≈ 0.5%. These sum to about 8%, consistent with the slice.

STEP 5 - Volume: A thin pizza slice is about 1.5 cm thick at the crust and thinner at the tip. Slice area ≈ 8% x 600 cm² ≈ 48 cm²; average height ≈ 1.2 cm gives ≈ 58 ml gross.
Split: crust ≈ 15 ml, sauce/cheese/toppings ≈ 43 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Bread-like crust 0.9 x 15 ml ≈ 14 g. Cheese and sauce mix, dense topping, ~0.9 x 43 ml ≈ 39 g, split as cheese ≈ 20 g and sauce ≈ 12 g, pepperoni ≈ 7 g.

STEP 7 - Energy (cooked weight):
- Crust: 14 g x 270 kcal/100 g ≈ 38 kcal
- Mozzarella cheese: 20 g x 300 kcal/100 g ≈ 60 kcal
- Tomato sauce: 12 g x 35 kcal/100 g ≈ 4 kcal
- Pepperoni: 7 g x 490 kcal/100 g ≈ 34 kcal

Total ≈ 53 g, ≈ 136 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: One thin slice of pepperoni pizza is typically 80–120 g and 250–300 kcal. This visible slice looks like a small, partly eaten piece with a bite missing, so ~53 g and ~136 kcal is on the low side but plausible for what is visible. The estimate is an approximation.
